note: Review of 14 articles (searched Feb-Jul 2019) covering 12 countries; its South African content is one paragraph drawn from a 2011 comparison, and the governance statement is made of the 11 countries collectively, not of South Africa by name.

facts.fact: The National Department of Health states that the District Health Management Information Systems (DHMIS) Policy for South Africa was adopted in July 2011 to make implementation uniform across the country, with standard operating procedures and a National Indicator Data Set governing data flow from facility to national level.

The National Digital Health Strategy 2019-2024, signed by the Minister of Health on 15 May 2019, names the DHIS as the routine system for tracking public-sector health service delivery, established in 1996/97, and as a component of the comprehensive HMIS the sector is working towards.

The strategy states that cutting primary healthcare registers from more than fifty to six standardised registers lightened the data capturing workload at facility level, and that South Africa has moved from DHIS 1.4 to WebDHIS; it dates neither, so the date is the strategy's signing.

The National Digital Health Strategy 2019-2024 makes a complete electronic health record its first digital health priority and commits to a roadmap for a national EHR that integrates existing solutions on a common platform, to be achieved by 2024.

The strategy is published by the National Department of Health, which it makes responsible for facilitating and coordinating implementation, including the electronic health record, by provinces, districts and municipalities.

The National Department of Health states that the diagnostic, treatment and billing modules needed for a patient electronic health record are yet to be developed, the patient registration system being only its first prerequisite.

facts.fact: The National Department of Health's bid terms of reference state that under the District Health Management Information System Policy the Director-General has overall ownership of the system, that all its data is owned by the Department of Health, and that every change to the system must be authorised by the department; the bidder may not share the data.

The National Department of Health itself invites bids, under National Treasury prescripts and priced in rand, for three years of hosting, maintenance, support and enhancement of the system; the bid names no funder other than the department and gives no contract value or budget line.

The department describes the system as an aggregated service delivery information system used at facility, district, province and national level, reporting by facility type (clinic, community health centre, hospitals), and plans user training at primary health care clinics, community health centres, district, regional and tertiary or central hospitals.

The department states that nine provincial instances capture the routine data while the national instance captures nothing directly and is filled by synchronisation; that the system offers offline entry by web or mobile; that all health facilities must reconcile source documents monthly against the databases they are captured into; and that 920 data capturers at primary health care clinics and 400 at district hospitals are to be trained over three years.

On 24 July 2026 the National Department of Health issued bid NDOH 09/2025-2026 (closing 25 August 2026) for a service provider to host, maintain, support and enhance the existing system for three years, covering nine provincial DHIS2 instances and the national data warehouse and competency-based training of about 6,000 officials (2,059 in year 1, 2,059 in year 2, 1,882 in year 3).

facts.fact: Thabethe and Mathews (University of the Western Cape) state that all public health facilities in Eastern Cape province use DHIS2 to collect and report routine health data; the province has 860 public facilities (727 primary health care clinics, 41 community health centres, 92 hospitals), of which 850 are registered in the national data dictionary and expected to report monthly. One province only; study period April 2017 to March 2020.

The authors state that clinicians record into patient records and tick registers, the data is consolidated monthly onto a facility input form, and it is then captured into DHIS2 by a dedicated, DHIS2-trained information cadre appointed or seconded in the health facility, citing the national department's 2012 and 2013 standard operating procedures. Eastern Cape, April 2017 to March 2020.

The authors state that all public health facilities in Eastern Cape use DHIS2, with capture by staff in the facility; in their sample of 265 of 850 facilities, 9,489 of 9,540 expected monthly reports were received (99.5%) over April 2017 to March 2020, while data-element completeness was 49.7% and overall data completeness 74.6%. The share is of all public facilities in one province, not of primary clinics nationally, and mobile clinics, satellite clinics and health posts were excluded from the sample.

The authors state that the National Department of Health decided in 2017 to upgrade from the standalone DHIS to DHIS2 and adopted it as the priority information system, and that the Eastern Cape Department of Health officially adopted online DHIS2 in 2017 on the national department's instruction.
